Living Well / Free resources

Notes, documents & useful information

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Capture a thought, locate a document, or keep a source without designing a complete personal operating system.

Information is useful when you can find it, understand its origin, and decide what to do with it. This collection separates notes, shared lists, scanning, diagrams, references, and ebook organization rather than calling them all productivity tools.

Start with: NAPS2: scan and arrange pages. Start with the official download and one test document, not a complete private archive.

Resources with a clear purpose.

Notes app · Free core app

Obsidian: local notes

Obsidian

A place for linked notes when keeping a readable personal collection matters more than building a dashboard.

Begin here: Create one short note before adding plugins or moving an existing archive.

Access: Core app is free without an account. Optional Sync and Publish services are paid. A compatible device is needed.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Obsidian: local notes

Context & source

Local files still need an appropriate backup. Plugins, sharing, and chosen sync services introduce their own permissions and data handling.

Public source information reviewed. No installation, account workflow, security audit, or personal-use result is claimed.

Notes and checklists · Free account for participation

Simplenote: a small shared note

Automattic

A lightweight option for plain notes and lists that need to appear on more than one device.

Begin here: Read the collaboration and export sections, then try one non-sensitive note.

Access: Free service; an account is required. Collaboration requires participants to have accounts.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Simplenote: a small shared note

Context & source

The provider says notes are not encrypted at rest and advises against sensitive content. Publishing a note makes it readable by anyone with its link.

Official how-to · Free to browse

Google Keep: collaboration basics

Google

Understand the difference between sending information and allowing someone to edit a note with you.

Begin here: Read what collaborators can change before sharing a low-stakes list.

Access: The guide is free to read. Using shared Keep notes requires suitable Google accounts and access to the service.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Google Keep: collaboration basics

Context & source

Deleting a shared note you own removes it for collaborators too. A shared checklist does not establish that another person accepted a responsibility.

Official how-to · Free to browse

Apple Notes: copy or collaborate

Apple

A useful decision point for a household plan: send a fixed copy, or maintain an editable shared version.

Begin here: Use the guide matching the software on the devices involved; compare the two sharing choices.

Access: Free instructions. Collaboration needs compatible Apple devices, Apple Accounts, and Notes enabled in iCloud.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Apple Notes: copy or collaborate

Context & source

Choose permissions deliberately and confirm the intended person can open the note. Device and storage costs are separate from the free guide.

Official how-to · Free to browse

Google Drive: scan a document

Google

An entry point for turning one ordinary paper document into a digital copy you can name and find.

Begin here: Scan a harmless sample and inspect every page before relying on the method.

Access: Free instructions; the mobile workflow needs a compatible device, Drive access, and available account storage.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open Google Drive: scan a document

Context & source

Check cropping, page order, legibility, and sharing. A searchable copy is not proof that every word was recognized correctly.

Document scanning · Free core app

NAPS2: scan and arrange pages

NAPS2 project

A desktop option for combining scans, rearranging pages, and creating searchable document copies.

Begin here: Start with the official download and one test document, not a complete private archive.

Access: Free open-source software for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Scanning requires compatible hardware and drivers.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open NAPS2: scan and arrange pages

Context & source

Inspect the saved page images and recognized text. Software cannot decide which consequential paper originals you may discard.

Citation tool · Free browser interactive

ZoteroBib: a one-off bibliography

Corporation for Digital Scholarship

Keep the sources behind a short piece of writing visible without starting a full research-library project.

Begin here: Read the FAQ, add one public source, and check its author, title, and date against the original.

Access: Free browser service without an account or installation. It uses browser storage; sharing a saved version uploads that version.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open ZoteroBib: a one-off bibliography

Context & source

A formatted citation does not verify a claim. Export work you need to keep, and avoid private information on shared computers.

Diagramming · Free browser interactive

draw.io: make an idea visible

draw.io

Turn a confusing sequence or small plan into a diagram that can be discussed and revised.

Begin here: Follow the basic editor introduction; draw three labeled boxes before exploring templates.

Access: Free browser editor without a required account; a desktop option is available. Some integrations and storage services have separate terms.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open draw.io: make an idea visible

Context & source

Choose where to save, retain an editable original, and add a text explanation for people who cannot use the diagram.

Ebook management · Free core app

calibre: organize an ebook collection

calibre project

Keep an existing ebook collection readable and organized instead of repeatedly searching for the same book.

Begin here: Try a legally obtained, unrestricted ebook and compare the library view with your existing folders.

Access: Free open-source desktop software; compatible hardware and lawful access to the books are required.

Perspective: Official product documentation; selected for a bounded everyday task.

Open calibre: organize an ebook collection

Context & source

Keep originals and check device and format compatibility. A management tool does not grant permission to copy or redistribute books.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Try one low-stakes item first. Keep an original, name the result plainly, and test finding or exporting it. A familiar folder or paper note remains a valid alternative.
